newsitem.title: THAILAND: Democrats accept reports NAP ahead in Thai poll.
newsitem.headline: Democrats accept reports NAP ahead in Thai poll.

text.p: The leader of the Democrat Party, former premier Chuan Leekpai, acknowledged late on Sunday unofficial projections that his party was trailing the New Aspiration Party (NAP) in the Thai election.

He was commenting on television and radio station reports, based on votes counted about six hours after polling closed, that the NAP led by Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh had overtaken the Democrats by a slim margin.

"According to the information that I have followed, the Democrat Party has not emerged as the number one party and therefore we will proceed to be in the opposition in the future...if the reports prove to be correct," he told reporters in his southern hometown in Trang.
Shortly after he spoke, the Channel 9 television station said his party was projected to win 124 seats to the 393-seat parliament, the same as for the NAP.
But Channel 3 television projected 128 for the NAP and 124 for the Democrats. Earlier, official Radio Thailand and Channel 7 television projected that the NAP had edged slightly past the Democrats.

Chuan said if the outcome of the polls was a tie between the NAP and the Democrats, his party would actively seek to form a new coalition government just as the NAP would. The party that could muster a coalition with the most seats in parliament would have the right to form the new government.
